operators.name: embedding_lookup_gelu
semantics: Computes x = self.embedding(x) followed by x = nn.GELU()(x).
Embedding lookup: out[i,j,k] = weight[ indices[i,j], k ].
Indices are int64 and must be within [0, num_embeddings - 1].
GELU applies elementwise with the exact erff approximation used by PyTorch: gelu(x) = 0.5 * x * (1 + erf(x / sqrt(2))).
The entire operation is a single custom CUDA kernel that writes each output element once.
Indices tensor may be on CPU if provided by the caller, but the binding moves it to CUDA before launching the kernel.
Weight tensor must already be on CUDA; the binding transfers it if necessary.
Input x has shape [256, 512], dtype int64, on CPU.
The first operation is embedding lookup using the model's embedding weight of shape [20000, 768] float32.
Output is a new CUDA tensor of shape [256, 512, 768], dtype float32, contiguous.
Each output element is copied from the embedding weight at row indices[i,j].
Applies GELU activation elementwise on the CUDA float32 tensor of shape [256, 512, 768].
Uses the exact PyTorch GELU formula: 0.5 * x * (1 + erf(x / sqrt(2))).
The output tensor has the same shape and dtype, device CUDA.
This step is fused with the embedding lookup in our custom operator, but semantically it is applied after lookup.
Returns the final tensor of shape [256, 512, 768], dtype float32, device CUDA.
